t: Architecture Decision Recorder - public implementations survey
title: Architecture Decision Recorder - public implementations survey
definition: Documents important design decisions and their rationale.
description:
This database surveys Architecture Decision Recorder as it exists in public practice: Documents important design decisions and their rationale. The records below name real tools with real track records, explain the techniques they are built on, cite the standards they implement, and provide drills that build working skill. Nothing here is speculative - every implementation is a real project you can download, every technique is established practice.

The value of a survey like this is comparative: seeing seven real implementations side by side reveals what the capability truly requires and where each tool draws its boundaries. The technique records go deeper, explaining the machinery - the algorithms, protocols and disciplines - that make Architecture Decision Recorder work regardless of which tool you pick.

Use this database as a field guide. When a build calls for Architecture Decision Recorder, consult the spotlights to choose an implementation, check the standards to stay interoperable, and run the drills to build fluency. Each record's demo program runs with node - the capability is demonstrated end to end.

t: Architecture Decision Recorder handoff protocol - practitioner discipline
title: Architecture Decision Recorder handoff protocol - practitioner discipline
definition: The handoff protocol discipline for Architecture Decision Recorder: documents important design decisions and their rationale..
description:
Good Architecture Decision Recorder practice is not talent - it is handoff protocol. It turns Architecture Decision Recorder from an event into a repeatable capability.

Concretely: verify outputs against the original request, not against your hopes; keep a failure log: what broke, why, and what now prevents it; review the result with fresh eyes before calling it done This record exists because the difference between a tool and a capability is discipline. Run the demo, adopt the checklist, and Architecture Decision Recorder becomes something your builds can rely on.
